rationale: Canonical namespace identity decides self-heritage. A namespaced InvalidArgumentException extending the global builtin has a real dependency even though both display leaves are equal. The native type-identity regression verifies this distinction. Heritage payloads mirror the emitted display spellings; canonical identities are stored separately.

expectSymbols.name: PlainIface
expectSymbols.note: An interface with no parents. ABSENT, and the row kills a payload that names a heritage this declaration does not have.

expectSymbols.name: WithBaseAndInterfaces
expectSymbols.note: THE row that separates a complete payload from a base-only one: an implementation that mirrors only `baseClass` passes every other row in this file and fails this one.

expectSymbols.name: WithInterfaceOnly
expectSymbols.note: Interfaces with no base — the arm a base-only implementation gets right by accident, so it is pinned separately from the row above rather than folded into it.

expectSymbols.name: DerivedIface
expectSymbols.note: An interface's parents are `extends` edges; the payload must carry them, or the walk stops exactly where a PHP codebase puts most of its interfaces.

expectSymbols.name: FeaturesForm
expectSymbols.note: Same leaf as its fully-qualified external base. The QUALIFICATION must survive into the payload: re-leafing would name a class after the one it started from.

expectSymbols.name: InvalidArgumentException
expectSymbols.note: Forms\Setup\InvalidArgumentException and the global InvalidArgumentException are different class identities.

expectRelationships.note: The edge the payload must MIRROR — same spelling, asserted on both sides so the two cannot drift apart.
The qualified same-leaf base. This row is what makes the payload row above a mirror rather than an independent re-derivation: both must carry the qualified string.
